# AGENTS.md — Workspace-level instructions for AI coding agents

> These rules apply to **all** AI-assisted contributions to `deepspeedai/DeepSpeed`.

## Contribution Policy (Mandatory)

### Duplicate-work checks

Before proposing a PR, run these checks:

```bash
gh issue view <issue_number> --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --comments
gh pr list --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --state open --search "<issue_number> in:body"
gh pr list --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --state open --search "<short area keywords>"
```

- If an open PR already addresses the same fix, do not open another.
- If your approach is materially different, explain the difference in the issue.
- DeepSpeed carries long-lived parallel implementations (ZeRO 1/2 vs 3, fp16 vs bf16 optimizers, per-accelerator op builders). Before fixing a bug in one, check whether the sibling paths share the defect, and state in the PR which ones you checked.

### New features need an accepted proposal first

Per [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md#new-feature-contribution-guidelines), a new feature starts with a proposal issue -- description, motivation, rough design, and planned experiments -- that maintainers accept before implementation begins. Do not open a feature PR with no accepted proposal; open the proposal issue instead.

### No low-value busywork PRs

Do not open one-off PRs for tiny edits (a single typo, an isolated style change, a lone type annotation). Mechanical cleanups are acceptable only when bundled with substantive work in the same area. This is the PR-level form of the rule against cosmetic changes below.

### Accountability

- Pure code-agent PRs are **not allowed**. A human submitter must understand and defend the change end-to-end.
- The submitting human must review every changed line and run the relevant tests.
- `Signed-off-by` is a [DCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developer_Certificate_of_Origin) attestation made by a person, not by an agent. Never sign off on a diff that no human has read.
- PR descriptions for AI-assisted work **must** include:
    - Why this does not duplicate an existing PR or issue.
    - Test commands run and their results, including the hardware they ran on: device model and count, accelerator/driver version, and torch version.
    - Convergence, throughput, and peak-memory results when the change affects numerics, performance, or memory -- see [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md#step-1-proposal-and-discussion) for the evidence bar.
    - Which cells of the compatibility matrix (ZeRO stage, offload, precision, parallelism) were validated, and which were not.
    - A clear statement that AI assistance was used.
- Before opening or reviewing a PR, work through the [`/pr-checklist`](.agents/skills/pr-checklist/SKILL.md) skill: design fit, accelerator portability, backward compatibility, on-device validation, diff hygiene, and PR contents.

### Fail-closed behavior

If the work is duplicate, trivial busywork, or an unproposed new feature, **do not proceed**. Return a short explanation of what is missing.

---

## DeepSpeed Project Rules

### Commit & CI requirements

- When creating commits, use `git commit --signoff`.
- DCO compliance is enforced by the required CI check; do not report commit-signoff findings in code reviews.
- Formatting: yapf (column_limit=119, `.style.yapf`) + flake8 (`.flake8`).
- Always verify changed files pass pre-commit checks before committing: `pre-commit run --files <changed_files>`. Only check modified files, not the entire codebase. Config: `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.
- `check-torchdist` hook: NEVER directly import torch's distributed module. Use `import deepspeed.comm as dist` instead.
- New source files (`.py`, `.c`/`.cpp`/`.cu`/`.h`, and the other extensions matched by the `check-license` hook) require license header:
  ```
  # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
  # DeepSpeed Team
  ```

### Code change discipline

- NEVER make cosmetic/formatting-only changes to existing code. Only add/modify lines that are functionally necessary. Minimizing diff noise is critical for code review.
- Delete dead code decisively — if code is unused at runtime (only referenced in tests), remove it along with its tests.
- Prefer consolidating tests over proliferating test files.
- Blend in: when modifying code, read the surrounding context and match the style of neighboring code (naming, spacing, patterns, idioms).
- Write beginner-friendly code: avoid deeply nested expressions or chained logic. Break complex expressions into clear, named intermediate steps.
- Comments should explain **why**, not **what**. Describe the purpose and reasoning, not the mechanics that the code already shows.
- New features must include corresponding tests and documentation updates.
- All changes must not cause `import deepspeed` to initialize CUDA; Keep heavy imports (> 0.1s) out of `import deepspeed`; Avoid changing `deepspeed/__init__.py` unless necessary.

### Test discipline

- Tests verify contracts, not implementations: a test is well-formed only if a different correct implementation of the same contract passes it.
- Before writing a test, name the concrete incorrect behavior it would catch; if you cannot name one, do not write it.
- Assert on observable outcomes through public/stable interfaces; do not assert private method return values or exact internal strings unless pinning a specific fixed bug (justify in a comment).
- Anchor to an external oracle or an independently derived reference instead of re-implementing the logic under test.
- Mocks must stand in for a collaborator's documented contract (schema, protocol), never for internals of the module under test.
- Changes that affect the external contract at the training-loop or inference level require integration tests, not just unit tests (e.g. a minimal training loop with `SimpleModel`).
- Integration tests must be executed on actual devices, not merely written: report the execution hardware spec and results in the PR.

## Tool Caveats

### Edit tool auto-formatter

The Edit tool has a hidden auto-formatter that silently changes quotes, whitespace, blank lines, and line wrapping. For format-sensitive modifications (e.g., when exact formatting matters for pre-commit), use `bash` with `sed`, `python`, or `cat` instead.

Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:

- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

# AGENTS.md — Workspace-level instructions for AI coding agents

> These rules apply to **all** AI-assisted contributions to `deepspeedai/DeepSpeed`.

## Contribution Policy (Mandatory)

### Duplicate-work checks

Before proposing a PR, run these checks:

```bash
gh issue view <issue_number> --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --comments
gh pr list --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --state open --search "<issue_number> in:body"
gh pr list --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --state open --search "<short area keywords>"
```

- If an open PR already addresses the same fix, do not open another.
- If your approach is materially different, explain the difference in the issue.
- DeepSpeed carries long-lived parallel implementations (ZeRO 1/2 vs 3, fp16 vs bf16 optimizers, per-accelerator op builders). Before fixing a bug in one, check whether the sibling paths share the defect, and state in the PR which ones you checked.

### New features need an accepted proposal first

Per [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md#new-feature-contribution-guidelines), a new feature starts with a proposal issue -- description, motivation, rough design, and planned experiments -- that maintainers accept before implementation begins. Do not open a feature PR with no accepted proposal; open the proposal issue instead.

### No low-value busywork PRs

Do not open one-off PRs for tiny edits (a single typo, an isolated style change, a lone type annotation). Mechanical cleanups are acceptable only when bundled with substantive work in the same area. This is the PR-level form of the rule against cosmetic changes below.

### Accountability

- Pure code-agent PRs are **not allowed**. A human submitter must understand and defend the change end-to-end.
- The submitting human must review every changed line and run the relevant tests.
- `Signed-off-by` is a [DCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developer_Certificate_of_Origin) attestation made by a person, not by an agent. Never sign off on a diff that no human has read.
- PR descriptions for AI-assisted work **must** include:
    - Why this does not duplicate an existing PR or issue.
    - Test commands run and their results, including the hardware they ran on: device model and count, accelerator/driver version, and torch version.
    - Convergence, throughput, and peak-memory results when the change affects numerics, performance, or memory -- see [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md#step-1-proposal-and-discussion) for the evidence bar.
    - Which cells of the compatibility matrix (ZeRO stage, offload, precision, parallelism) were validated, and which were not.
    - A clear statement that AI assistance was used.
- Before opening or reviewing a PR, work through the [`/pr-checklist`](.agents/skills/pr-checklist/SKILL.md) skill: design fit, accelerator portability, backward compatibility, on-device validation, diff hygiene, and PR contents.

### Fail-closed behavior

If the work is duplicate, trivial busywork, or an unproposed new feature, **do not proceed**. Return a short explanation of what is missing.

---

## DeepSpeed Project Rules

### Commit & CI requirements

- When creating commits, use `git commit --signoff`.
- DCO compliance is enforced by the required CI check; do not report commit-signoff findings in code reviews.
- Formatting: yapf (column_limit=119, `.style.yapf`) + flake8 (`.flake8`).
- Always verify changed files pass pre-commit checks before committing: `pre-commit run --files <changed_files>`. Only check modified files, not the entire codebase. Config: `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.
- `check-torchdist` hook: NEVER directly import torch's distributed module. Use `import deepspeed.comm as dist` instead.
- New source files (`.py`, `.c`/`.cpp`/`.cu`/`.h`, and the other extensions matched by the `check-license` hook) require license header:
  ```
  # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
  # DeepSpeed Team
  ```

### Code change discipline

- NEVER make cosmetic/formatting-only changes to existing code. Only add/modify lines that are functionally necessary. Minimizing diff noise is critical for code review.
- Delete dead code decisively — if code is unused at runtime (only referenced in tests), remove it along with its tests.
- Prefer consolidating tests over proliferating test files.
- Blend in: when modifying code, read the surrounding context and match the style of neighboring code (naming, spacing, patterns, idioms).
- Write beginner-friendly code: avoid deeply nested expressions or chained logic. Break complex expressions into clear, named intermediate steps.
- Comments should explain **why**, not **what**. Describe the purpose and reasoning, not the mechanics that the code already shows.
- New features must include corresponding tests and documentation updates.
- All changes must not cause `import deepspeed` to initialize CUDA; Keep heavy imports (> 0.1s) out of `import deepspeed`; Avoid changing `deepspeed/__init__.py` unless necessary.

### Test discipline

- Tests verify contracts, not implementations: a test is well-formed only if a different correct implementation of the same contract passes it.
- Before writing a test, name the concrete incorrect behavior it would catch; if you cannot name one, do not write it.
- Assert on observable outcomes through public/stable interfaces; do not assert private method return values or exact internal strings unless pinning a specific fixed bug (justify in a comment).
- Anchor to an external oracle or an independently derived reference instead of re-implementing the logic under test.
- Mocks must stand in for a collaborator's documented contract (schema, protocol), never for internals of the module under test.
- Changes that affect the external contract at the training-loop or inference level require integration tests, not just unit tests (e.g. a minimal training loop with `SimpleModel`).
- Integration tests must be executed on actual devices, not merely written: report the execution hardware spec and results in the PR.

The Edit tool has a hidden auto-formatter that silently changes quotes, whitespace, blank lines, and line wrapping. For format-sensitive modifications (e.g., when exact formatting matters for pre-commit), use `bash` with `sed`, `python`, or `cat` instead.

5	DeepSpeed 不只跑在 NVIDIA GPU 上。读完本讲，你应该能够：

13	## 2. 前置知识
14	
15	- **硬件后端（backend）**：DeepSpeed 把「一块可以执行张量计算的设备」抽象为 accelerator，例如 `cuda`（NVIDIA GPU）、`cpu`、`hpu`（Habana Gaudi）、`xpu`（Intel GPU）、`npu`（华为昇腾）、`klxpu`（昆仑芯 XPU）等。PyTorch 本身为每种硬件提供一组 `torch.cuda.*` / `torch.xpu.*` 风格的 API，但名字各不相同。
16	- **ABC 抽象基类**：Python 的 `abc.ABC` + `@abc.abstractmethod` 定义「子类必须实现」的接口。抽象方法只写 `...`（函数体为空），实现类必须逐一落实。
17	- **全局单例**：`real_accelerator.py` 用模块级全局变量 `ds_accelerator` 缓存当前选中的后端实例，首次 `get_accelerator()` 时探测并构造，之后直接复用。
18	- **pinned memory（页锁定主机内存）**：普通主机内存可能被操作系统换页（page out），设备异步 DMA 拷贝期间内存被搬走会得到脏数据。pinned memory 被锁在物理页上，且能被设备直接映射进设备页表，是高速 H2D/D2H 拷贝和 ZeRO-Offload 的基础。CUDA 里对应 `cudaHostRegister`/`cudaHostUnregister`。
19	- **CUDA Graph（图捕获）**：把一段 GPU 操作录制（capture）成一张图，之后一次 replay 就重放全部操作，省去逐 kernel 的 launch 开销。图捕获期间很多 host 端调用（如查询、同步）是非法的，所以「是否正处于捕获中」本身也需要一个查询接口。DeepSpeed 的 Hybrid Engine 用它加速推理 rollout（详见 u7-l4）。
20	- **ctypes / FFI**：Python 标准库 `ctypes` 可以直接 `CDLL` 加载动态库（如 `libze_loader.so.1`）、按 C 结构体布局定义 `Structure`、声明函数签名后直接调用 C 函数——不需要写任何 C 扩展。
21	- **符号链接双轨布局**（u1-l2 已建立）：git 实际跟踪的是仓库顶层的 `accelerator/` 目录；`deepspeed/accelerator` 是一个指向 `../accelerator/` 的符号链接。两个导入路径（`accelerator.xxx` 与 `deepspeed.accelerator.xxx`）解析到同一份源码文件，但在 Python 里是两个独立模块对象。

39	## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

41	### 4.1 模块一：AbstractAccelerator——设备无关接口的总纲
42	
43	#### 4.1.1 概念说明
44	
45	DeepSpeed 的 runtime 代码（engine、ZeRO、通信……）要同时支持十种硬件，但它不想在任何业务文件里写 `if backend == "cuda": torch.cuda.xxx() elif ...`。解决办法是一层**端口-适配器（port-adapter）抽象**：
46	
47	- `DeepSpeedAccelerator` 是「端口」，用抽象方法声明所有运行时需要的设备能力；
48	- 每种硬件的后端类（`CUDA_Accelerator`、`CPU_Accelerator`……）是「适配器」，把这些方法映射到各自的 torch 原生 API；
49	- 业务代码统一通过 `get_accelerator().xxx()` 调用，从此不知道脚下是哪种硬件。
50	
51	接口分两类：
52	
53	1. **`@abc.abstractmethod` 抽象方法**：每个后端必须实现，否则实例化时报错；
54	2. **带默认实现的「能力位 / 钩子」**：基类给出保守默认值（多数为 `False` 或空操作），后端**验证通过后显式覆写**才开启——`is_fp64_supported`、`prefer_triton_grouped_mm`、`is_graph_capture_supported`、`register_host_memory` 都属于这一类。
55	
56	#### 4.1.2 核心流程
57	
58	后端类实现接口的判定流程可以概括为：
59	
60	```text
61	新后端 XYZ 接入
62	  ├─ 必须实现：全部 @abstractmethod（设备/RNG/流/内存/类型/图/张量/算子构建）
63	  ├─ 能力位逐项决定：
64	  │    ├─ 默认值（False / 空操作）→ 保守路径
65	  │    └─ 覆写为 True → 上层功能随之开启
66	  └─ get_accelerator() 校验 isinstance(XYZ_Accelerator, DeepSpeedAccelerator)
67	       通过 → 单例缓存，全局使用
68	```

145	#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

147	**练习 1**：为什么 `is_fp64_supported` 不是抽象方法，而是带默认实现 `return True`？
148	**答案**：见 [accelerator/abstract_accelerator.py:L177-L179](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/84679e9d3a2582bffc53a5259d13cfc7278c9772/accelerator/abstract_accelerator.py#L177-L179) 的注释——几乎所有加速器都支持 fp64，只有少数不支持的后端才需要覆写；把它做成抽象方法会强迫所有后端写一模一样的样板代码。这也是抽象层的一个通用取舍：**越是「几乎人人都有」的能力越适合给默认实现，越是「人人不同」的能力越适合抽象方法**。

151	**答案**：探测器把实例缓存在模块级全局变量 `ds_accelerator`（见 4.2.3），首次构造后复用。后端对象自身带有状态（如 CUDA 的 pynvml 句柄、CPU 的 max_mem 统计），反复新建既浪费又会重复初始化原生库。
152

154	**答案**：`False` 表示「该后端不支持把已有主机内存注册进设备页表，但流程可以继续」——上层（原生 pinned memory 通道）据此回退到 mlock-only 的保守实现。抛异常则会让「后端不支持」变成「功能崩溃」。能力位钩子的约定是**报能力、不报错误**。

156	### 4.2 模块二：real_accelerator——运行时探测器
157	
158	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
159	
160	`get_accelerator()` 要回答一个问题：**当前进程该用哪个后端类？** 它按两级策略决定：
161	
162	1. **显式覆盖**：环境变量 `DS_ACCELERATOR=klxpu` 直接指定，并**预检对应的 torch 扩展是否安装**（装不上就立刻报 `ValueError`，而不是等到运行中神秘崩溃）；
163	2. **自动探测**：依次尝试导入各硬件的 torch 扩展（`torch_npu`、`torch_sdaa`、`habana_frameworks`、`torch_mlu`、`torch_supa`、`torch_xmlir`……），谁导入成功就用谁，最后兜底 `cpu`。
164	
165	探测完成后构造单例并做 `isinstance` 校验。
166	
167	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
168	
169	```text
170	get_accelerator()
171	  ├─ 全局 ds_accelerator 已有？ → 直接返回（缓存）
172	  ├─ ① DS_ACCELERATOR 环境变量？
173	  │     ├─ 在 SUPPORTED_ACCELERATOR_LIST 中 → 预检扩展可用性 → accelerator_name 确定
174	  │     └─ 非法值 → ValueError
175	  ├─ ② 自动探测（按固定顺序逐个 try-import）
176	  │     xpu(torch.xpu) → npu → sdaa → mps → hpu → mlu
177	  │     → supa → klxpu → cuda → 全部失败 → cpu（打 warning）
178	  ├─ ③ 按 accelerator_name import 对应后端类并实例化
179	  ├─ ④ _validate_accelerator：isinstance 双基类校验
180	  └─ 日志 "Setting ds_accelerator to <name> (<override|auto detect>)"

349	### 4.4 模块四：图捕获能力的显式 opt-in 声明（含 KLXPU 演进，#9042）
350	
351	#### 4.4.1 概念说明
352	
353	图捕获（CUDA Graph capture）是 Hybrid Engine 推理加速的关键路径（u7-l4 详述），但它在图录制期间有严格限制：很多 host 端查询（同步、某些张量检查）在捕获中是**非法**的，调用会直接报错。因此 DeepSpeed 把「支持图捕获」设计成一个**显式 opt-in 的能力位**，而不是「实现了 create_graph 就等于支持」：

355	- 基类默认 `is_graph_capture_supported() -> False`：只暴露图 API 形状的后端（如 CPU）留在 eager 路径；

470	### 4.5 模块五：XPU 的 Level Zero pinned memory 注册——绕过 torch 的自力更生
471	
472	#### 4.5.1 概念说明
473	
474	pinned memory 的「注册」语义：把一块**已经存在**的主机内存（例如原生 pinned 后端用 mlock 锁住的缓冲）映射进设备页表，使设备 DMA 可以直接安全访问它。CUDA 有 `cudaHostRegister`，但 Intel GPU 的 torch 通道（`torch.xpu`）**没有暴露等价 API**。XPU 后端的解法是：既然 torch 不给通道，就直接用 `ctypes` 加载 Level Zero 的用户态驱动加载器 `libze_loader.so.1`，走 `ZE_extension_external_memmap_sysmem` 扩展完成同一件事。
475	
476	这是后端适配里「**torch 通道不可用时自力更生**」的典型模式：
477	
478	1. 用 `ctypes.CDLL` 直接加载厂商驱动库；
479	2. 按 C 头文件手写结构体布局与函数签名（`ze_api.h` 的稳定 ABI）；
480	3. 可选扩展先探测（probe）再使用，失败路径一律降级（warn_once + 回退 mlock-only），绝不崩溃。
481	
482	#### 4.5.2 核心流程
483	
484	```text
485	register_host_memory(address, num_bytes)   ← 原生 pinned 通道调用（4.1.3 的分发层）
486	  ├─ _l0_device_context(current_device())
487	  │    ├─ _l0_loader()                       （lru_cache 全局一次）
488	  │    │    CDLL("libze_loader.so.1")
489	  │    │    zeInit → zeDriverGet
490	  │    │    zeDriverGetExtensionProperties 探测
491	  │    │      "ZE_extension_external_memmap_sysmem" 不在 → None（不可用）
492	  │    │    声明 zeMemAllocHost / zeMemFree 等签名
493	  │    └─ 按 UUID 匹配 torch 设备 → zeContextCreateEx 单设备上下文
494	  │         （多设备上下文只映射首个设备的页表 → 其他设备拷贝报
495	  │          OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY，故必须单设备上下文；
496	  │          设备页表跨上下文共享，映射后任何上下文可用）
497	  ├─ 无 Level Zero → warning_once + return False（回退 mlock-only）
498	  ├─ zeMemAllocHost(host_desc ⇐ memmap_desc → pSystemMemory=address)
499	  │    ├─ rc != SUCCESS → warning_once + return False
500	  │    └─ mapped != address（非恒等映射）→ zeMemFree + return False
501	  └─ 记录 (_l0_registrations[address]) → return True
502	
503	unregister_host_memory(address)
504	  └─ zeMemFree(context, address)；失败 → raise RuntimeError
505	     （保持 CPU 分配存活，防止释放驱动仍映射的页）
506	```

535	| CUDA / 通用概念 | Level Zero 对应（源码位置） |
536	| --- | --- |
537	| 驱动加载 | `ctypes.CDLL("libze_loader.so.1")`（L70） |
538	| `cudaHostRegister(ptr, size, flags)` | `zeMemAllocHost` + memmap 扩展描述符链（L409-L417） |

541	| 可选能力探测 | `zeDriverGetExtensionProperties`（L89-L103） |
542	
543	2. 在**任意机器**（包括 CPU）上梳理失败路径：`_l0_loader()` 第一步 `CDLL` 就会因找不到 `libze_loader.so.1` 返回 `None`，随后 `_l0_device_context` 返回 `None`，最终 `register_host_memory` 打出 warning_once「Level Zero host-memory registration is unavailable ... native pinned memory stays mlock-only」并返回 `False`。用下列**示例代码**在 CPU 上验证这条降级链不需要任何 Intel 硬件：
544	
545	```python

547	from deepspeed.accelerator.cpu_accelerator import CPU_Accelerator

551	# 该行为需要 torch.xpu 环境，待本地验证。
552	```
553	
554	3. 对照 4.1.3 的分发层（abstract_accelerator.py L337-L352）画出完整调用图：`accelerator.pin_memory(t)` → 原生 pinned 通道（`DS_PIN_MEMORY_BACKEND` 启用时）→ `register_host_memory(addr, nbytes)` → Level Zero 或 mlock-only。
555	
556	**需要观察的现象**：第 2 步在 CPU 上返回 `False` 且不抛异常；如果你在 Intel GPU 机器上运行（装好 torch.xpu 与 Level Zero），应看到注册返回 `True`、`_l0_registrations` 里出现一条记录（待本地验证）。
557	
558	**预期结果**：你总结出的模式应当是——**探测（probe）先行、可选能力不假设、失败路径全部有降级、资源注销失败宁可报错也不静默**。这四条同样适用于你为任何新硬件写后端适配。
559	
560	#### 4.5.5 小练习与答案
561	
562	**练习 1**：为什么 `_l0_loader` 与 `_l0_device_context` 都加 `lru_cache`，而 `_l0_registrations` 是普通 dict？
563	**答案**：前两者是**纯函数式的环境事实**——加载器句柄与设备上下文在进程内不变，缓存避免每次注册都重复 `CDLL`/`zeInit`/UUID 扫描。`_l0_registrations` 是**可变状态**（注册了什么、注销了什么随运行变化），必须允许修改，dict 按地址作为 key 记账（L174、L433、L437）。
564	
565	**练习 2**：`register_host_memory` 要求恒等映射（返回指针 == 输入指针），为什么这是硬性要求？
566	**答案**：调用方（原生 pinned 通道）已经持有并继续使用**原始**指针——张量数据结构里存的就是它。若驱动返回一个搬了家的映射地址，设备访问映射区与 host 访问原地址会落在两块内存上，数据悄无声息地不一致；而调用方无法整体换用新地址。所以非恒等映射只能释放掉并按「不可用」降级（L424-L432 的注释原文：callers hold the original pointer）。
567	
568	**练习 3**：注册失败走 warning + 降级，注销失败却 raise，这个不对称合理吗？
569	**答案**：合理，按「失败后能否安全继续」划分。注册失败 = 功能缺失，mlock-only 的 pinned 内存仍然正确（少了设备页表映射的性能收益），可以继续跑；注销失败 = 驱动可能仍持有对这段主机内存的映射，此时把 CPU 侧内存释放掉，后续任意写入都可能污染尚在进行的设备 DMA——静默继续是不安全的，报错让上层保留分配（L442-L447 注释）才是安全默认。

581

586	    "comm_backend": a.communication_backend_name(),
587	    "is_synchronized_device": a.is_synchronized_device(),
588	    "use_host_timers": a.use_host_timers(),
589	    "graph_capture_supported": a.is_graph_capture_supported(),
590	    "bf16": a.is_bf16_supported(),
591	    "fp16": a.is_fp16_supported(),
592	    "fp64": a.is_fp64_supported(),
593	    "triton": a.is_triton_supported(),
594	    "prefer_triton_grouped_mm": a.prefer_triton_grouped_mm(),
595	    "total_memory_bytes": a.total_memory(),
596	    "available_memory_bytes": a.available_memory(),
597	    "device_count": a.device_count(),

600	    print(f"{k:28s} = {v}")
601	
602	# ② 图操作契约：CPU 上应是「假捕获 + 空回放」
603	import torch
604	g = a.create_graph()
605	print("create_graph() ->", g)            # CPU: None
606	t = torch.zeros(1)

608	    t.fill_(1.0)                          # 捕获体立即 eager 执行
609	print("after capture:", t.item())         # 1.0
610	a.replay_graph(g)                         # 空操作，不报错
611	print("after replay:", t.item())          # 仍是 1.0
612	
613	# ③ set_accelerator 替换单例（模拟扩展包注册自定义后端）
614	class MyCPUAccelerator(CPU_Accelerator):
615	    def __init__(self):
616	        super().__init__()
617	        self._name = "mycpu"
618

620	set_accelerator(mine)
621	print("swapped to:", get_accelerator()._name)   # mycpu
622	```
623

625	
626	1. 把报告输出与 4.3.4 的对照表并排，逐项确认 CPU 列与源码一致；
627	2. 对照 4.4 的契约解释 `graph_capture_supported=False` 时脚本②的行为为什么是「安全降级」而非「功能缺失报错」；

630	**预期结果**：CPU 环境下脚本全绿；③证明单例可替换且替换经过 `_validate_accelerator` 双基类校验。GPU/XPU 环境下同一脚本输出的差异（`nccl`、`graph_capture_supported=True`、pynvml 口径显存、Level Zero 注册成功）即为各后端语义差异的活样本（待本地验证）。

632	## 6. 本讲小结
633	
634	- **抽象层的形状**：`DeepSpeedAccelerator` 用约 20 组、60+ 个方法覆盖设备/RNG/流/内存/类型/图/张量/pinned memory/算子构建；抽象方法强制「人人实现」，能力位（`is_graph_capture_supported`、`prefer_triton_grouped_mm`、`register_host_memory`…）默认保守值、后端显式 opt-in。

636	- **参照实现的取舍**：CUDA 直连 `torch.cuda`（pynvml 空闲显存、nccl、真图捕获），CPU 全面退化（psutil + cgroup 口径、ccl/gloo、`None` 图 + eager 空操作）；`is_synchronized_device` 一个事实派生出计时/依赖/反压三个问题。

638	- **自力更生模式**：XPU 在 torch 无对应通道时用 ctypes 直驱 Level Zero——lru_cache 的加载器、可选扩展先探测、UUID 匹配设备、单设备上下文、恒等映射校验、失败一律 warn + 降级、注销失败宁可报错。
639	
640	## 7. 下一步学习建议

644	- **u7-l4（Hybrid Engine）**：本讲的 `is_graph_capture_supported` 在那里被两条生成路径消费（回退 eager 的 warning 就来自那里），静态 KV cache 与 `is_current_stream_capturing` 的配合也将展开。

# 加速器抽象层：一套代码支持多种硬件

## 1. 本讲目标

DeepSpeed 不只跑在 NVIDIA GPU 上。读完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 列举 `AbstractAccelerator`（`DeepSpeedAccelerator`）定义的 20+ 组设备无关接口，并按「设备 / RNG / 流与事件 / 显存 / 数据类型 / 图操作 / 张量 / pinned memory / 算子构建」分组归类。
2. 解释 `real_accelerator.py` 的探测加载机制：`DS_ACCELERATOR` 环境变量覆盖优先，其次按「装了哪个 torch 扩展」自动探测，探测顺序为什么必须把「伪装成 torch.cuda 的后端」放在 CUDA 之前。
3. 以 CUDA 与 CPU 两个参照实现为例，对比同一接口在不同硬件上的语义差异（同步设备、可用内存、通信后端、图捕获）。
4. 解释图捕获能力的**显式 opt-in** 设计：`is_graph_capture_supported()` 默认 `False`，后端验证通过后才覆写为 `True`；KLXPU 如何从「显式拒绝」演进到「继承 CUDA 的 opt-in」（#9042）。
5. 以 XPU 后端为例，看一个 accelerator 如何绕过 torch、用 `ctypes` 直接驱动 Level Zero 的 `ZE_extension_external_memmap_sysmem` 扩展注册页锁定主机内存——「torch 通道不可用时后端自力更生」的实现模式。

## 2. 前置知识

- **硬件后端（backend）**：DeepSpeed 把「一块可以执行张量计算的设备」抽象为 accelerator，例如 `cuda`（NVIDIA GPU）、`cpu`、`hpu`（Habana Gaudi）、`xpu`（Intel GPU）、`npu`（华为昇腾）、`klxpu`（昆仑芯 XPU）等。PyTorch 本身为每种硬件提供一组 `torch.cuda.*` / `torch.xpu.*` 风格的 API，但名字各不相同。
- **ABC 抽象基类**：Python 的 `abc.ABC` + `@abc.abstractmethod` 定义「子类必须实现」的接口。抽象方法只写 `...`（函数体为空），实现类必须逐一落实。
- **全局单例**：`real_accelerator.py` 用模块级全局变量 `ds_accelerator` 缓存当前选中的后端实例，首次 `get_accelerator()` 时探测并构造，之后直接复用。
- **pinned memory（页锁定主机内存）**：普通主机内存可能被操作系统换页（page out），设备异步 DMA 拷贝期间内存被搬走会得到脏数据。pinned memory 被锁在物理页上，且能被设备直接映射进设备页表，是高速 H2D/D2H 拷贝和 ZeRO-Offload 的基础。CUDA 里对应 `cudaHostRegister`/`cudaHostUnregister`。
- **CUDA Graph（图捕获）**：把一段 GPU 操作录制（capture）成一张图，之后一次 replay 就重放全部操作，省去逐 kernel 的 launch 开销。图捕获期间很多 host 端调用（如查询、同步）是非法的，所以「是否正处于捕获中」本身也需要一个查询接口。DeepSpeed 的 Hybrid Engine 用它加速推理 rollout（详见 u7-l4）。
- **ctypes / FFI**：Python 标准库 `ctypes` 可以直接 `CDLL` 加载动态库（如 `libze_loader.so.1`）、按 C 结构体布局定义 `Structure`、声明函数签名后直接调用 C 函数——不需要写任何 C 扩展。
- **符号链接双轨布局**（u1-l2 已建立）：git 实际跟踪的是仓库顶层的 `accelerator/` 目录；`deepspeed/accelerator` 是一个指向 `../accelerator/` 的符号链接。两个导入路径（`accelerator.xxx` 与 `deepspeed.accelerator.xxx`）解析到同一份源码文件，但在 Python 里是两个独立模块对象。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| [docs/_tutorials/accelerator-abstraction-interface.md](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/84679e9d3a2582bffc53a5259d13cfc7278c9772/docs/_tutorials/accelerator-abstraction-interface.md) | 官方移植指南：`torch.cuda.xxx` → `get_accelerator().xxx` 的改写规则与图捕获 opt-in 契约 |

> 注意：`deepspeed/accelerator/` 在仓库里是符号链接（`ls -la deepspeed/` 可见 `accelerator -> ../accelerator/`），git 只跟踪顶层 `accelerator/`。因此本文永久链接统一使用 `accelerator/...` 这一真实路径；你在代码里看到 `from deepspeed.accelerator.cuda_accelerator import ...` 时，读到的就是同一个文件。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 模块一：AbstractAccelerator——设备无关接口的总纲

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

DeepSpeed 的 runtime 代码（engine、ZeRO、通信……）要同时支持十种硬件，但它不想在任何业务文件里写 `if backend == "cuda": torch.cuda.xxx() elif ...`。解决办法是一层**端口-适配器（port-adapter）抽象**：

- `DeepSpeedAccelerator` 是「端口」，用抽象方法声明所有运行时需要的设备能力；
- 每种硬件的后端类（`CUDA_Accelerator`、`CPU_Accelerator`……）是「适配器」，把这些方法映射到各自的 torch 原生 API；
- 业务代码统一通过 `get_accelerator().xxx()` 调用，从此不知道脚下是哪种硬件。

接口分两类：

1. **`@abc.abstractmethod` 抽象方法**：每个后端必须实现，否则实例化时报错；
2. **带默认实现的「能力位 / 钩子」**：基类给出保守默认值（多数为 `False` 或空操作），后端**验证通过后显式覆写**才开启——`is_fp64_supported`、`prefer_triton_grouped_mm`、`is_graph_capture_supported`、`register_host_memory` 都属于这一类。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

后端类实现接口的判定流程可以概括为：

```text
新后端 XYZ 接入
  ├─ 必须实现：全部 @abstractmethod（设备/RNG/流/内存/类型/图/张量/算子构建）
  ├─ 能力位逐项决定：
  │    ├─ 默认值（False / 空操作）→ 保守路径
  │    └─ 覆写为 True → 上层功能随之开启
  └─ get_accelerator() 校验 isinstance(XYZ_Accelerator, DeepSpeedAccelerator)
       通过 → 单例缓存，全局使用
```

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

类的骨架与四个「同步设备」行为接口：

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 `is_fp64_supported` 不是抽象方法，而是带默认实现 `return True`？

**练习 2**：`get_accelerator()` 返回的对象为什么不每次新建？
**答案**：探测器把实例缓存在模块级全局变量 `ds_accelerator`（见 4.2.3），首次构造后复用。后端对象自身带有状态（如 CUDA 的 pynvml 句柄、CPU 的 max_mem 统计），反复新建既浪费又会重复初始化原生库。

**练习 3**：`register_host_memory` 的默认返回值是 `False` 而不是抛 `NotImplementedError`，这传递了什么设计意图？
**答案**：`False` 表示「该后端不支持把已有主机内存注册进设备页表，但流程可以继续」——上层（原生 pinned memory 通道）据此回退到 mlock-only 的保守实现。抛异常则会让「后端不支持」变成「功能崩溃」。能力位钩子的约定是**报能力、不报错误**。

### 4.2 模块二：real_accelerator——运行时探测器

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

`get_accelerator()` 要回答一个问题：**当前进程该用哪个后端类？** 它按两级策略决定：

1. **显式覆盖**：环境变量 `DS_ACCELERATOR=klxpu` 直接指定，并**预检对应的 torch 扩展是否安装**（装不上就立刻报 `ValueError`，而不是等到运行中神秘崩溃）；
2. **自动探测**：依次尝试导入各硬件的 torch 扩展（`torch_npu`、`torch_sdaa`、`habana_frameworks`、`torch_mlu`、`torch_supa`、`torch_xmlir`……），谁导入成功就用谁，最后兜底 `cpu`。

探测完成后构造单例并做 `isinstance` 校验。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

```text
get_accelerator()
  ├─ 全局 ds_accelerator 已有？ → 直接返回（缓存）
  ├─ ① DS_ACCELERATOR 环境变量？
  │     ├─ 在 SUPPORTED_ACCELERATOR_LIST 中 → 预检扩展可用性 → accelerator_name 确定
  │     └─ 非法值 → ValueError
  ├─ ② 自动探测（按固定顺序逐个 try-import）
  │     xpu(torch.xpu) → npu → sdaa → mps → hpu → mlu
  │     → supa → klxpu → cuda → 全部失败 → cpu（打 warning）
  ├─ ③ 按 accelerator_name import 对应后端类并实例化
  ├─ ④ _validate_accelerator：isinstance 双基类校验
  └─ 日志 "Setting ds_accelerator to <name> (<override|auto detect>)"
```

探测顺序是**有序的**，两条注释专门解释了两处顺序敏感：`torch_supa` 和 `torch_xmlir`（KLXPU）都会**把自己伪装成 torch.cuda**（即 `torch.cuda.is_available()` 会为真），所以它们的检查必须排在真正的 CUDA 检查之前，否则会被误判成 `cuda` 后端。

#### 4.2.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 `DS_ACCELERATOR=klxpu` 时要在探测器里 `import torch_xmlir`，而不是等后端类用到时再失败？
**答案**：显式指定后端的用户预期「配错了立刻知道」。预检把「扩展未安装」从运行中段的随机位置提前到 `get_accelerator()` 首次调用处，错误信息也带修复建议（装 torch_xmlir）。这是 fail-fast 原则在配置边界的应用。

**练习 2**：把 `klxpu` 的探测分支移到 `cuda` 分支之后会发生什么？
**答案**：由于 `torch_xmlir` 会以 torch.cuda 的面目呈现（`torch.cuda.device_count() > 0 and torch.cuda.is_available()` 为真），CUDA 分支会先命中，`accelerator_name` 被定为 `cuda`，KLXPU 后端永远不会被自动选中——这正是源码注释「must come before the CUDA detection below」守护的场景。顺序本身就是协议的一部分。

**练习 3**：为什么第 ③ 步实例化用一串延迟 `import` 而不是文件顶部统一 import 全部 10 个后端类？
**答案**：顶部统一 import 意味着「使用 CUDA 的机器也必须装 torch_npu、habana_frameworks 等全部扩展」——任何一个缺失都会让 `import deepspeed` 直接失败。延迟导入保证只有被选中的后端（及其依赖）才被加载，也顺带满足了「import deepspeed 不得做重活」的项目纪律（见 AGENTS.md：import 不得初始化 CUDA、重导入要避免）。

### 4.3 模块三：两个参照实现——CUDA 与 CPU

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

`CUDA_Accelerator` 是「最完整」的实现：直连 `torch.cuda`，能展示接口的全部语义。`CPU_Accelerator` 则演示**接口的退化艺术**：没有设备、没有流的硬件上，每个接口仍要给出语义正确的答案（哪怕答案是 `None` 或空操作）。两个实现对照着读，最能看清抽象边界画在哪里。

KLXPU 等后端更进一步：**直接继承 `CUDA_Accelerator`**，只覆写差异点（见 4.4 节）——因为 `torch_xmlir` 把整套 torch.cuda API 都接管了。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

读这对实现的固定套路：

```text
对每个接口问三个问题
  1. 委托给谁？（torch.cuda.xxx / torch.xpu.xxx / psutil / 返回常量）
  2. 语义差异是什么？（同步 vs 异步、真实设备 vs 主机进程）
  3. 错误/缺失时怎么办？（pynvml 不在 → 回退 total - allocated）
```

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

先看构造函数里两个重要字段：

- [accelerator/cuda_accelerator.py:L29-L37](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/84679e9d3a2582bffc53a5259d13cfc7278c9772/accelerator/cuda_accelerator.py#L29-L37)：CUDA 后端 `_name='cuda'`，通信后端为 `'nccl'`（Windows 下降级 `'gloo'`），编译后端 `"inductor"`；pynvml 延迟初始化（CUDA 不可用时 import 也不炸）。
- [accelerator/cpu_accelerator.py:L165-L179](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/84679e9d3a2582bffc53a5259d13cfc7278c9772/accelerator/cpu_accelerator.py#L165-L179)：CPU 后端的通信后端是 `'ccl'`（装了 oneccl 绑定时）或 `'gloo'`，并用 `psutil` 记录进程 RSS 作为内存统计基础。

**对比一：执行模型四连问。**

- [accelerator/cuda_accelerator.py:L51-L61](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/84679e9d3a2582bffc53a5259d13cfc7278c9772/accelerator/cuda_accelerator.py#L51-L61)：CUDA 答 `is_synchronized_device() == False`，其余三个方法全部转发给它——GPU 异步执行，所以计时要用设备事件、数据依赖要显式 stream 同步、显存反压要自己处理。

#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：`CPU_Accelerator.device()` 返回 `None` 而不是 `torch.device('cpu')`，为什么上层没有崩？
**答案**：见 [accelerator/cpu_accelerator.py:L198-L199](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/84679e9d3a2582bffc53a5259d13cfc7278c9772/accelerator/cpu_accelerator.py#L198-L199)。接口约定「返回当前设备对象」，而 CPU 场景下张量创建惯用 `device=get_accelerator().current_device_name()`（即字符串 `'cpu'`）或默认设备；`None` 传给 torch 的多数 API 恰好表示「默认设备」。约定俗成的配合点，移植新后端时要照抄语义而不是照抄返回值。

**练习 2**：CUDA 的 `available_memory` 为什么不直接用 `torch.cuda.mem_get_info()` 之类的 torch API，而引入 pynvml？
**答案**：pynvml 给的是**驱动视角的整机空闲显存**（包含其他进程占用的排除），torch 的 allocated 统计只算本进程张量缓存池。对「还差多少显存才能放得下参数分区」这类问题，驱动口径更接近真相；pynvml 缺失时才退回 `total - allocated` 的近似（L203-L204）。代价是必须处理 pynvml 与 torch 的设备编号不一致（`_get_nvml_gpu_id` 的 `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` 重映射，L181-L194）。

**练习 3**：`use_host_timers` 为什么等于 `is_synchronized_device`？
**答案**：异步设备上 host 时钟与 kernel 执行不对齐——host 记时的起止点之间 GPU 可能还在排队，测出来的「耗时」包含排队噪声。同步设备（CPU）上计算与时钟同源，host 计时既准又便宜。所以这组派生关系（L54-L55、L185-L186）把「用哪种计时」归约到「设备是否同步」这一个事实上。KLXPU 后端覆写 `use_host_timers` 的理由也在此：它的 CUDA 事件计时器默认返回 0.0，不得不用 host 计时（见 4.4.3）。

### 4.4 模块四：图捕获能力的显式 opt-in 声明（含 KLXPU 演进，#9042）

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

图捕获（CUDA Graph capture）是 Hybrid Engine 推理加速的关键路径（u7-l4 详述），但它在图录制期间有严格限制：很多 host 端查询（同步、某些张量检查）在捕获中是**非法**的，调用会直接报错。因此 DeepSpeed 把「支持图捕获」设计成一个**显式 opt-in 的能力位**，而不是「实现了 create_graph 就等于支持」：

- 基类默认 `is_graph_capture_supported() -> False`：只暴露图 API 形状的后端（如 CPU）留在 eager 路径；
- 后端必须**同时**实现 `is_current_stream_capturing()`（供静态 KV cache 等组件在捕获期间跳过非法的 host 端检查），并经验证后才覆写为 `True`；
- 该能力**可被继承**，所以「继承自 CUDA 但尚未验证」的子类必须显式覆写回 `False`（default-deny）。

KLXPU 正是这条规则的标准案例：它继承 `CUDA_Accelerator`（因为 `torch_xmlir` 接管了 torch.cuda API），图捕获未经验证期间在子类里显式 `return False`；#9042 完成验证后**删除了这个覆写**，于是随 CUDA 一起进入图捕获路径。整个演进过程中，「是否支持」始终是后端自己显式声明的决定，而不是隐式继承的副作用。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

```text
上层想用图捕获（HybridEngine 图缓存 / rollout 生成路径）
  └─ 查 get_accelerator().is_graph_capture_supported()
       ├─ True  → 走图捕获路径
       │          （捕获期间组件用 is_current_stream_capturing()
       │            跳过 host 端检查）
       └─ False → warning_once + 回退 eager 生成（不报错）

后端侧的生命周期：
  暴露图 API（create_graph/capture_to_graph/replay_graph）   ← 必须实现（抽象）
  实现 is_current_stream_capturing                            ← opt-in 前提
  验证通过 → 覆写 is_graph_capture_supported = True           ← 显式 opt-in
  继承自已 opt-in 的基类但未验证 → 子类显式覆写回 False        ← default-deny
  验证完成 → 删除子类覆写，恢复继承                            ← KLXPU 的 #9042
```

### 4.5 模块五：XPU 的 Level Zero pinned memory 注册——绕过 torch 的自力更生

#### 4.5.1 概念说明

pinned memory 的「注册」语义：把一块**已经存在**的主机内存（例如原生 pinned 后端用 mlock 锁住的缓冲）映射进设备页表，使设备 DMA 可以直接安全访问它。CUDA 有 `cudaHostRegister`，但 Intel GPU 的 torch 通道（`torch.xpu`）**没有暴露等价 API**。XPU 后端的解法是：既然 torch 不给通道，就直接用 `ctypes` 加载 Level Zero 的用户态驱动加载器 `libze_loader.so.1`，走 `ZE_extension_external_memmap_sysmem` 扩展完成同一件事。

这是后端适配里「**torch 通道不可用时自力更生**」的典型模式：

1. 用 `ctypes.CDLL` 直接加载厂商驱动库；
2. 按 C 头文件手写结构体布局与函数签名（`ze_api.h` 的稳定 ABI）；
3. 可选扩展先探测（probe）再使用，失败路径一律降级（warn_once + 回退 mlock-only），绝不崩溃。

#### 4.5.2 核心流程

```text
register_host_memory(address, num_bytes)   ← 原生 pinned 通道调用（4.1.3 的分发层）
  ├─ _l0_device_context(current_device())
  │    ├─ _l0_loader()                       （lru_cache 全局一次）
  │    │    CDLL("libze_loader.so.1")
  │    │    zeInit → zeDriverGet
  │    │    zeDriverGetExtensionProperties 探测
  │    │      "ZE_extension_external_memmap_sysmem" 不在 → None（不可用）
  │    │    声明 zeMemAllocHost / zeMemFree 等签名
  │    └─ 按 UUID 匹配 torch 设备 → zeContextCreateEx 单设备上下文
  │         （多设备上下文只映射首个设备的页表 → 其他设备拷贝报
  │          OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY，故必须单设备上下文；
  │          设备页表跨上下文共享，映射后任何上下文可用）
  ├─ 无 Level Zero → warning_once + return False（回退 mlock-only）
  ├─ zeMemAllocHost(host_desc ⇐ memmap_desc → pSystemMemory=address)
  │    ├─ rc != SUCCESS → warning_once + return False
  │    └─ mapped != address（非恒等映射）→ zeMemFree + return False
  └─ 记录 (_l0_registrations[address]) → return True

unregister_host_memory(address)
  └─ zeMemFree(context, address)；失败 → raise RuntimeError
     （保持 CPU 分配存活，防止释放驱动仍映射的页）
```

#### 4.5.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 `_l0_loader` 与 `_l0_device_context` 都加 `lru_cache`，而 `_l0_registrations` 是普通 dict？
**答案**：前两者是**纯函数式的环境事实**——加载器句柄与设备上下文在进程内不变，缓存避免每次注册都重复 `CDLL`/`zeInit`/UUID 扫描。`_l0_registrations` 是**可变状态**（注册了什么、注销了什么随运行变化），必须允许修改，dict 按地址作为 key 记账（L174、L433、L437）。

**练习 2**：`register_host_memory` 要求恒等映射（返回指针 == 输入指针），为什么这是硬性要求？
**答案**：调用方（原生 pinned 通道）已经持有并继续使用**原始**指针——张量数据结构里存的就是它。若驱动返回一个搬了家的映射地址，设备访问映射区与 host 访问原地址会落在两块内存上，数据悄无声息地不一致；而调用方无法整体换用新地址。所以非恒等映射只能释放掉并按「不可用」降级（L424-L432 的注释原文：callers hold the original pointer）。

**练习 3**：注册失败走 warning + 降级，注销失败却 raise，这个不对称合理吗？
**答案**：合理，按「失败后能否安全继续」划分。注册失败 = 功能缺失，mlock-only 的 pinned 内存仍然正确（少了设备页表映射的性能收益），可以继续跑；注销失败 = 驱动可能仍持有对这段主机内存的映射，此时把 CPU 侧内存释放掉，后续任意写入都可能污染尚在进行的设备 DMA——静默继续是不安全的，报错让上层保留分配（L442-L447 注释）才是安全默认。

## 6. 本讲小结

- **抽象层的形状**：`DeepSpeedAccelerator` 用约 20 组、60+ 个方法覆盖设备/RNG/流/内存/类型/图/张量/pinned memory/算子构建；抽象方法强制「人人实现」，能力位（`is_graph_capture_supported`、`prefer_triton_grouped_mm`、`register_host_memory`…）默认保守值、后端显式 opt-in。
- **探测协议**：`DS_ACCELERATOR` 覆盖优先（带扩展预检、非法值 fail-fast），否则按固定顺序 try-import 自动探测；`torch_supa`/`torch_xmlir` 会伪装成 torch.cuda，必须在 CUDA 之前检查；结果缓存在全局单例，`set_accelerator` 可替换并经双基类 isinstance 校验（符号链接双轨布局的必然产物）。
- **参照实现的取舍**：CUDA 直连 `torch.cuda`（pynvml 空闲显存、nccl、真图捕获），CPU 全面退化（psutil + cgroup 口径、ccl/gloo、`None` 图 + eager 空操作）；`is_synchronized_device` 一个事实派生出计时/依赖/反压三个问题。
- **图捕获是显式声明而非隐式继承**：基类默认 `False`；CUDA/NPU 验证后 opt-in 且必须先实现 `is_current_stream_capturing`；消费方（rollout、图缓存）查到不支持就 warning + 回退 eager。KLXPU 先 default-deny、#9042 验证后删除覆写恢复继承——支持与否始终是后端自己的显式决定。
- **自力更生模式**：XPU 在 torch 无对应通道时用 ctypes 直驱 Level Zero——lru_cache 的加载器、可选扩展先探测、UUID 匹配设备、单设备上下文、恒等映射校验、失败一律 warn + 降级、注销失败宁可报错。

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.
